method: Re-read the dated study-abroad entry and official catalogue payload, then verified the five replacement course codes, credits, periods and prerequisites independently of the draft totals. Rechecked the dated Biblical Hebrew and thesis entry conditions before reconsidering the frozen curriculum, workbook trials and reader-facing text.
findings: The dated study-abroad entry expressly permits a five-module local pathway for students unable to travel. It does not require the local option to follow the Prague eligibility rule. The five dated courses total 30 EC in periods four and five and replace the 30 EC abroad component without duplicate credit. The reconstructed first, second and third years each total 60 EC.

Biblical Hebrew begins with lectures in block five, alongside Modern Hebrew 4. The intermediate sequence and Ulpan prerequisites are met in order, and year-one Biblical Hebrew prepares for Bible (+ source texts). The subject-specific requirements precede the 12 EC thesis. The taught content and conflicting Ulpan title warrant no CEFR-level claim.

The strongest feasible UCR trials bring real value through comparative literature, historical source work, ancient material culture, Mediterranean art, institutions and conflict. The workbook does not support connected Hebrew source work or sustained historical, religious, intellectual and modern social study of Jewish communities. The regional direction also lacks cumulative Middle Eastern study. This disposition follows programme-level testing, independently of offerings, and is not based solely on the absence of Hebrew instruction.

The external-only view shows all 24 verified components, the selected major, 30 EC genuine choice and targeted progression notes. The text qualifies the local pathway and does not assign a location or level to the replaced semester. There are no selected UCR course descriptions.
